properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued October 18 at 12:59AM PDT until October 20 at 9:00AM PDT by NWS San Diego CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents and breaking waves due to elevated
surf expected. Surf will build to 3 to 6 feet Sunday and persist
through Tuesday morning.

* WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas and Orange County
Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...From 9 AM PDT this morning through Tuesday morning.

* IMPACTS...There is an increased risk of ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Waves can
wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats
nearshore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Minor beach erosion and tidal overflows may
occur across south-facing beaches, especially in the Huntington
Beach area.
properties.instruction:
Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous swimming conditions, or
stay near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly
in such conditions, stay off the rocks.

* IMPACTS...Very steep and hazardous seas could capsize or cause
damage to vessels.

feet after midnight.

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 9 to 12
feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip
currents.

* WHERE...East and south facing reefs of Tinian and Saipan.

* WHEN...Until 4 AM ChST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Significant and dominant south-southwesterly
swell generated by distant Typhoon Champi (29W) and secondary
northeasterly swell generated by distant remnants of Koguma and
associated frontal systems will produce hazardous surf and
dangerous rip currents along east and south facing reefs.

should remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions.

current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: Tropical Cyclone Local Statement issued October 18 at 5:51PM ChST until October 18 at 8:00PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
...SUPER TYPHOON CHAMPI CONTINUES WESTWARD AWAY FROM GUAM
WATERS...
...TYPHOON WARNING IS CANCELLED FOR GUAM AND ROTA...

.NEW INFORMATION...
Warnings have been discontinued.

.AREAS AFFECTED...
This local statement provides important information and
recommended actions for people in Guam and the Northern Marianas.

.Watches/Warnings...
Tropical cyclone watches and warnings are no longer in effect
anywhere across the Marianas and surrounding waters.

A Flood Watch is in effect for portions of Guam and the Northern
Marianas. Please listen closely for any Flood Warnings that might
be in effect for your area.

Please check the latest public and marine forecasts for detailed
information about additional hazards.

.STORM INFORMATION...
At 5 PM ChST...the center of Super Typhoon Champi (29W) was
located near latitude 13.0N...longitude 142.3E. This was about
170 miles west of Guam. Storm motion was west, 270 degrees, at
10 mph. Storm intensity was 150 mph.

.SITUATION OVERVIEW...
Super Typhoon Champi (29W) continues westward away from Guam coastal
waters with the eye fully obscured by cloud cover in latest visible
satellite imagery, as it looks to be going through an eyewall
replacement cycle. Heavy rainbands extend outward roughly 100 miles
east of the center to the edge of western Guam coastal waters, with
additional bands roughly 250 miles and 400 miles outward to the east
and southwest. Locally heavy showers continue to move north-northwest
across Marianas coastal waters along the outer periphery of Champi,
and continue to produce near-gale to gale-force gusts, as fresh to
strong southeast to south winds persist in the wake of Champi.
properties.instruction:
Remain in suitable shelter until the all clear has been given.
Passing showers may still produce sudden, gale-force wind gusts.

Pay attention for possible road closures and stay away from
downed power lines. Listen for any boil water alerts.

Mariners should check the latest coastal waters forecast before
making any definite plans.

NWSheadline: TYPHOON WARNING IS CANCELLED

properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued October 18 at 3:24AM EDT until October 20 at 5:00PM EDT by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, 2 to 4 feet of
inundation above ground level expected in low- lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the High Surf
Advisory, large breaking waves of 9 to 14 feet in the surf
zone. For the Beach Hazards Statement, dangerous rip currents,
large breaking waves, and strong longshore currents in the
surf zone.

* WHERE...Hatteras Island.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, until 5 PM EDT Tuesday.
For the Beach Hazards Statement, from Sunday morning through
Sunday evening.

* IMPACTS...2 to 4 feet of inundation above ground level is
expected in some areas near shorelines and tidal waterways
resulting in an elevated threat of property damage. Flooding
will extend inland from the waterfront threatening some homes
and businesses. Numerous road closures and flooding of
vehicles will be possible. Vulnerable portions of NC-12 may be
inundated, especially around high tide. There is a possibility
of being stranded on Hatteras Island for multiple days. This
could be life threatening if you have an emergency. Dangerous
swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach erosion.
Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore
into deeper water. Dangerous shore break can throw a swimmer
or surfer head first into the bottom causing neck and back
injuries. Strong longshore currents will create dangerous
swimming conditions.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...This has the potential to be a long
duration event bringing more significant ocean overwash impacts
to vulnerable oceanside areas through multiple high tide cycles
into the work week. Minor soundside water level rises will also
be possible.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Swimmers should remain out of the water due to dangerous surf
conditions.

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, two to four feet of

shorelines and tidal waterways. For the High Surf Advisory,
large breaking waves of 8 to 10 feet expected in the surf
zone. For the Beach Hazards Statement, dangerous rip currents,
large breaking waves expected, and strong longshore currents
in the surf zone.

* WHERE...Ocracoke Island.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, until 5 PM EDT Tuesday.
For the High Surf Advisory, from midnight tonight to 8 PM EDT
Monday. For the Beach Hazards Statement, from Sunday morning
through Sunday evening.

* IMPACTS...Up to 2 to 4 feet of inundation above ground level is
expected in some areas near shorelines and tidal waterways
resulting in an elevated threat of property damage. Flooding
will extend inland from the waterfront threatening some homes
and businesses. Numerous road closures and flooding of vehicles
will be possible. Vulnerable portions of NC-12 may be inundated,
especially around high tide. There is a possibility of being
stranded on Ocracoke for multiple days. This could be life
threatening if you have an emergency. Dangerous swimming and
surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. Rip currents can
sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
Dangerous shore break can throw a swimmer or surfer head first
into the bottom causing neck and back injuries. Strong longshore
currents will create dangerous swimming conditions.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...This has the potential to be a long
duration event bringing more significant ocean overwash impacts
to vulnerable oceanside areas through multiple high tide cycles
into the work week. Minor soundside water level rises will also
be possible.

water of unknown depth.

conditions.
